title: Counterexamples to the Corsten-Frankl conjecture on diameter-Ramsey simplices
summary: Corsten and Frankl conjectured that a simplex is diameter-Ramsey if and only if its circumcenter lies in its convex hull. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge 3$. The main tool is a sufficient criterion based on a higher-order deficit decomposition: if the squared deficits $D^2-\|p_i-p_j\|^2$ admit a nonnegative decomposition over subsets of the vertex set, with total mass at most $D^2$, then the simplex is diameter-Ramsey.
